newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Nayarit state coffee zones hit by broca.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Nayarit state coffee zones hit by broca.

text.p: Mexico's western state of Nayarit has seen a spreading of the notorious berry borer disease in its coffee plantations, state news agency Notimex reported Friday.
Citing Pablo Ramirez Escobedo, chairman of Nayarit Coffee Growers Association, Notimex said around 2,500 hectares are infected by broca of the 18,700 hectares under cultivation in the state.
Ramirez said that in 1995 when broca was first found in Nayarit, only around 600 hectares were infected. In 1996, the surface area infected totaled 1,400 hectares, he added.

Nayarit, one of several second-tier coffee growing states in Mexico, saw its output dip by around 20 percent in 1996-1997 cycle because of the berry borer disease, Ramirez said. He gave no specific production figures.
